_note: Both tools are self-validators: they parse a config and exit non-zero with a diagnostic, which is exactly the `validator` shape jq and virt-xml-validate already use. Only the VALIDATION subcommands appear here — `sing-box check` and `xray test`, never `run`, which would bind ports and touch the network. Shape detection is a two-clause lookahead rather than a filename glob because both tools eat `*.json`: a file qualifies only if it has an `inbounds` array AND that dialect's protocol vocabulary, so a sing-box config is never handed to xray or vice versa.

tools.name: xray
tools._note: `run -test` is xray's ONLY validation path — there is no `xray test` subcommand (the previous agent documented one; it exits `unknown command`, which a naive port turns into a finding claiming the user's config is malformed). `-test` loads and checks the config and exits WITHOUT launching the server: 0 on success printing `Configuration OK.`, 23 on a bad config. Per-FILE (`-c`) rather than per-directory (`-confdir`): -confdir parses every JSON in the directory, so it would hand a sing-box config to xray and report the dialect mismatch as an xray error.
